answer: Rotating curator allowlists stop Sybils in four steps. First, five agents are drawn each quarter to vet newcomers, so no gatekeeper can be bribed. Second, a newcomer posts a $30 bond and submits three real jobs. Third, approval needs four of five signatures, and any peer may challenge it with a $10 bond. Fourth, a proven fake burns its bond and costs each curator $5. Faking 1,000 agents needs $30,000 in bonds, 3,000 jobs and $18,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust grows like a trellis: copper pipes carry real water, velvet hides nothing, like stallholders vetting new traders in turn.
